best_for: Rust developers who already like JetBrains editors and want Cargo, a debugger and a test runner wired in, free for side projects and paid once the code earns money.
description:
RustRover is the Rust IDE from JetBrains, the company behind IntelliJ IDEA and PyCharm. JetBrains built it for Rust from the start instead of piecing it together from add-ons. It is also part of the All Products Pack, one subscription that covers 10 JetBrains IDEs.

If you are new to Rust, JetBrains Academy courses let you learn the language inside the IDE. You can manage Cargo workspaces, pick a keymap that suits you, and add features through plugins. Every tool works without AI. If you do use AI, JetBrains says your prompts go only to the provider you pick, and its own detailed AI data collection is off unless you turn it on.

points.title: Free unless you are paid
points.text: Non-commercial use is free for individuals. It needs a JetBrains Account sign-in, renews yearly only if you used it in the last 6 months, and sends anonymous usage statistics that cannot be switched off under that license.

points.title: Commercial prices
points.text: Individuals pay USD 69 per year or USD 6.90 a month. Organizations pay USD 229 per user per year or USD 22.90 a month. A 30-day trial is offered. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Cargo and the usual tools inside
points.text: Cargo, Clippy and rustfmt are built in, with Rust inspections, a one-click debugger and test runner, and code insight that follows types into macros. Web and database tools are included too.

points.title: Bring your own AI
points.text: You can connect agents such as Junie, Claude Agent, Codex or GitHub Copilot, and pick JetBrains AI, your own API key or a local model. None of it is required to use the IDE.

points.title: A heavy install
points.text: JetBrains asks for 8 GB of RAM with 3 GB free for the IDE and 10 GB of disk. The Flatpak alone is about 1.4 GB to download and about 4.1 GB installed.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is not JetBrains'
points.text: The Flathub build lists JetBrains as developer but Flathub does not mark it as verified, and JetBrains' install guide recommends its Toolbox App, a tarball or Snap instead. Supported desktops are Windows 10 and 11, macOS 26 and 27, and recent Ubuntu, Fedora and Debian.

points.title: Versions kept
points.text: Windows and macOS list every stable release since 2024.1, for x64 and Arm64, with the ones winget and Homebrew lack taken from JetBrains' own release feed. Windows installers run per user or machine-wide. Linux lists only the current release, so a Linux downgrade needs another source.
